newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar to pause before new slide.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar to pause before new slide.

text.p: The dollar is likely to trade sideways in the near term, but gloom and doom remains in store for the U.S. currency on the medium horizon, chartists said on Thursday.
"Dollar/yen went through 115.00," said technical analyst Ture Johnson at Bank of America, referring to the dollar's dip on Thursday to a five-month low of 114.70.

"From 115.00 through 114.50 is a very big level for dollar/yen because that's where the dollar rise accelerated last year," Johnson added. "We tested 115.00 (then) a couple of times and went straight to 127.00 or so."
In New York on Thursday, the dollar closed at 115.75/85 yen, down from 117.30/40 on Wednesday, with an intra-session low at 115.40 -- 12 yen below the dollar/yen rally peaked at 127.45 on May 1.

"So, 115.00 is going to be a very big level on the downside. "If we were to close below 114.50, the dollar would go straight down," Johnson predicted. "At some point, the dollar will have to digest its losses. It'll be choppy, sideways trading before the next breakdown."
Johnson said the dollar outlook was bearish as well versus the mark and other European currencies.

"It's a dollar/yen-related move. Dollar/yen led the move up, two years ago. It will lead again and dollar/Europe will lag. It's all driven by dollar/yen, then dollar/Swiss and the big lag will be dollar/mark," Johnson predicted.
"Dollar/mark has a bit of a range here, 1.6850 to 1.71 the figure, or maybe 1.7150, near term. But I think we'll see 1.6650 or 1.66 the figure," Johnson added.

The Bank of America analyst said it would take a dollar/mark close above 1.72 to jumpstart a fresh rally "that would make new highs" -- and would not be accompanied by a rise of the same magnitude on dollar/yen.
Analyst Scott Siller at MCM CurrencyWatch noted the breach of 115.00-yen support may not be convincing because "we went through 115.00 and within one hour, we were back to 115.95."
"We may be forming the right shoulder of a little base and go back to 117.50/60, the previous low," said Siller who remained "short-term bullish, but long-term bearish."

"My target is 111.25 yen, the low on July 8th," added the MCM analyst who professed to be bearish as well on dollar/mark "unless we move above 1.7040," a key level in a falling resistance line, and bearish on dollar/Swiss until 1.4385.
